questions.explanation_english: Section 37 of the POCSO Act, 2012 explicitly mandates that 'The Special Court shall try cases in camera and in the presence of the parents of the child or any other person in whom the child has trust or confidence.' In camera proceedings mean closed-door hearings conducted away from the public eye. Members of the public, extraneous individuals, and media reporters are strictly excluded from the courtroom. This statutory privacy protects the child's identity, preserves dignity, and minimizes distress during testimony.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 37 स्पष्ट रूप से यह अधिदेश देती है कि विशेष न्यायालय मामलों का विचारण बंद कमरे (इन कैमरा / In camera) में करेगा, जिसमें बच्चे के माता-पिता या ऐसा कोई अन्य व्यक्ति उपस्थित रहेगा जिस पर बच्चा विश्वास या भरोसा करता हो। 'इन कैमरा' विचारण का अर्थ है कि न्यायालय कक्ष में आम जनता और मीडिया का प्रवेश पूर्णतः वर्जित होता है। इसका उद्देश्य कार्यवाही की गोपनीयता बनाए रखना, बच्चे की पहचान और गरिमा की रक्षा करना तथा उसे अदालत के तनावपूर्ण माहौल से बचाना है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (b) In camera, with only permitted individuals present

questions.question_english: Which specific statutory provision of the POCSO Act, 2012 explicitly mandates that the Special Court must ensure that the child victim is not called repeatedly to testify in court?
options_english: Section 19 of the Act
Section 24 of the Act
Section 33(5) of the Act
Section 42 of the Act
questions.explanation_english:
Section 33 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 outlines the special procedure and powers of the Special Court.
Specifically, Section 33(5) states: 'The Special Court shall ensure that the child is not called repeatedly to testify in the court.'
This statutory safeguard is designed to prevent secondary victimization, reduce witness fatigue and anxiety, and ensure that trial procedures remain child-friendly. Other provisions mentioned:
- Section 19 deals with the mandatory reporting of offences.
- Section 24 covers the recording of a child's statement by police.
- Section 42 deals with alternative punishments under other laws.
Therefore, Section 33(5) is the exact provision protecting the child from repeated summons and appearances.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 33 विशेष न्यायालय की प्रक्रिया और शक्तियों का वर्णन करती है।
विशेष रूप से, धारा 33(5) स्पष्ट प्रावधान करती है: 'विशेष न्यायालय यह सुनिश्चित करेगा कि बालक को न्यायालय में गवाही (साक्ष्य) देने के लिए बार-बार न बुलाया जाए।' (The Special Court shall ensure that the child is not called repeatedly to testify in the court.)
इस प्रावधान का मूल उद्देश्य बालक को द्वितीयक उत्पीड़न (secondary victimization) और गंभीर मानसिक तनाव से बचाना है ताकि न्यायालय की प्रक्रिया बाल-सुलभ (child-friendly) बनी रहे।
अन्य विकल्प:
- धारा 19: अपराधों की अनिवार्य रिपोर्टिंग से संबंधित है।
- धारा 24: पुलिस द्वारा बालक के बयान दर्ज करने की प्रक्रिया से संबंधित है।
- धारा 42: अन्य कानूनों के तहत वैकल्पिक दंड से संबंधित है।
अतः सही प्रावधान धारा 33(5) है। इसलिए विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (c) Section 33(5)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 33(5) mandates that the Special Court shall ensure that the child victim is not called repeatedly to testify in court. Minimizing court appearances shields minor witnesses from repeated questioning, reduces emotional anxiety, and strictly upholds child-friendly procedural safeguards throughout all formal judicial trial proceedings.

questions.question_english: Upon completing an inquiry under the POSH Act, 2013 and arriving at a finding that the allegations of sexual harassment are proved, can the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) recommend financial compensation/penalty against the respondent?
options_english: Yes, by recommending deduction of monetary compensation from the respondent's salary or wages to be paid to the aggrieved woman.
No, the committee's powers are strictly limited to recommending a written reprimand, counseling, or transfer.
Yes, but the statutory maximum compensation that can be levied is strictly capped at Rs. 10,000 only.
No, any monetary compensation or financial penalty can only be ordered by a competent criminal court.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 13(3) of the POSH Act, 2013, where the Internal Committee arrives at the conclusion that the allegation against the respondent has been proved, it shall recommend to the employer:
1. To take disciplinary action for sexual harassment as a misconduct in accordance with the applicable service rules;
2. To deduct from the salary or wages of the respondent such sum as it may consider appropriate to be paid to the aggrieved woman or to her legal heirs, in accordance with the determination of compensation under Section 15 of the Act.
If the employer is unable to deduct such compensation due to respondent's absence from duty or cessation of employment, the committee may direct the respondent to pay such sum directly, and upon default, it can be recovered as an arrear of land revenue (Section 13(3)(ii)). There is no arbitrary Rs. 10,000 cap; Section 15 outlines factors like mental trauma, medical expenses, lost career opportunities, and the financial status of the respondent.
questions.explanation_hindi:
POSH अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 13(3) के अनुसार, यदि आंतरिक समिति (ICC) इस निष्कर्ष पर पहुंचती है कि प्रत्यर्थी पर आरोप सिद्ध हो चुके हैं, तो वह नियोक्ता को निम्नलिखित सिफारिश कर सकती है:
1. सेवा नियमों के अनुसार कदाचार (misconduct) के लिए अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई करना;
2. प्रत्यर्थी के वेतन या पारिश्रमिक से ऐसी उचित राशि की कटौती करके व्यथित महिला (या उसके विधिक वारिसों) को मुआवजा देना, जैसा धारा 15 के तहत निर्धारित किया गया हो।
यदि प्रत्यर्थी के वेतन से कटौती संभव न हो, तो समिति प्रत्यर्थी को सीधे भुगतान करने का निर्देश दे सकती है, तथा भुगतान न करने पर इसे भू-राजस्व के बकाए (arrear of land revenue) की भांति वसूला जा सकता है। धारा 15 में मानसिक आघात, चिकित्सा व्यय और पक्षों की वित्तीय स्थिति के आधार पर मुआवजे का निर्धारण होता है (इसकी ₹10,000 की कोई सीमा नहीं है)। अतः विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (a) Yes, by directing deduction of compensation from salary

questions.question_english: A school employs an external outsourced agency for transport services. A bus conductor sexually harasses a student. As per POCSO guidelines for schools, who is accountable for reporting this incident and ensuring safety protocols were in place?
options_english: Only the private transport agency owner managing the service
The School Management and Principal
The biological parents of the child involved in the incident
The local traffic police department having jurisdiction
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 19(1) of the POCSO Act, 2012, any person, including school authorities, heads of educational institutions, and management, who has apprehension or knowledge that an offence under the Act has been committed, has an absolute mandatory duty to report it immediately to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or the local police. Failure to report constitutes a criminal offence under Section 21. Furthermore, under CBSE Safety Guidelines, Ministry of Education directives, and NCPCR School Safety Manuals, the institutional leadership (School Management and Principal) remains strictly accountable for student safety in outsourced school transport. The school cannot abdicate its legal duty of care to a third-party vendor; it must ensure rigorous background verification of transport personnel, install CCTV/GPS, deploy female bus attendants, and immediately report any offence to law enforcement authorities.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 19(1) के अनुसार, यदि किसी विद्यालय के प्राचार्य, शिक्षक या प्रबंधन को किसी बालक के विरुद्ध लैंगिक अपराध की जानकारी या आशंका होती है, तो उसका यह अनिवार्य सांविधिक दायित्व है कि वह तुरंत पुलिस या विशेष किशोर पुलिस इकाई (SJPU) को इसकी सूचना दे। धारा 21 के तहत सूचना न देना या छिपाना दंडनीय अपराध है। इसके अतिरिक्त, सीबीएसई सुरक्षा दिशा-निर्देशों और एनसीपीसीआर सुरक्षा मानकों के अनुसार, परिवहन सेवा आउटसोर्स होने पर भी विद्यालय प्रबंधन और प्राचार्य छात्र सुरक्षा के दायित्व से मुक्त नहीं हो सकते। संविदा कर्मियों का अनिवार्य पुलिस सत्यापन कराना, बसों में सीसीटीवी/जीपीएस लगाना, महिला अटेंडेंट तैनात करना और घटना की तत्काल पुलिस रिपोर्ट दर्ज कराना विद्यालय प्रबंधन और प्राचार्य का प्रत्यक्ष कानूनी दायित्व है। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The School Management and Principal

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: School management and administrative heads remain accountable for ensuring overall safety protocols, including background verification of outsourced transport personnel. Upon learning of an offence committed by contractual transport staff, institutional leadership holds a statutory legal duty under Section 19 to report the matter to police immediately without delay.

questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 2(o) of the POSH Act, 2013, the term 'workplace' has an expansive, inclusive definition (concept of 'notional extension of workplace'). It includes any department, organization, undertaking, establishment, or any place visited by the employee arising out of or during the course of employment, including transportation provided by the employer.
Judicial precedents (including landmark High Court and Supreme Court rulings such as Sanjeev Mishra v. Bank of Baroda and others) have affirmed that virtual working environments, official video conferences, digital messaging platforms, and work-from-home arrangements are an extension of the workplace during the course of employment. Therefore, electronic or virtual sexual harassment occurring during remote work is fully cognizable by the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) under the POSH Act.

questions.explanation_english: Section 11 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 defines the offence of 'Sexual Harassment' upon a child. Under Section 11(i), a person is said to commit sexual harassment if, with sexual intent, they utter any word, make any sound or gesture, or exhibit any object or part of the body with the intention that such word, sound, gesture, object, or body part shall be heard or seen by the child. Because this act involves exhibiting a body part without physical penetrative contact, it does not constitute penetrative sexual assault under Section 3 or aggravated assault under Section 5, but falls squarely within the statutory definition of sexual harassment under Section 11.

questions.question_english: Which of the following correctly states the statutory limitation period for filing a complaint of sexual harassment under Section 9(1) of the POSH Act, 2013?
options_english: Within 30 days from the date on which the alleged incident occurred
Within 3 months of the incident or last incident in a series
Within 6 months from the date on which the alleged incident occurred
Within 1 year from the date on which the alleged incident occurred
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 9(1) of the POSH Act, 2013, the limitation period for filing a complaint is strictly codified as follows:
'Any aggrieved woman may make, in writing, a complaint of sexual harassment at workplace to the Internal Committee if so constituted, or the Local Committee, in case it is not so constituted, within a period of three months from the date of incident and in case of a series of incidents, within a period of three months from the date of last incident.'

Key Principles:
1. Isolated Incident: The complaint must be made within three months from the date of the occurrence.
2. Continuing Misconduct / Series of Incidents: Where an employee is subjected to ongoing harassment, the three-month period begins from the date of the last occurrence in that sequence.
3. Statutory Extension: The ICC may extend this period by another three months under the second proviso to Section 9(1) if sufficient cause prevented timely filing.

Thus, option (B) accurately states the limitation period.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 9(1) के अंतर्गत कार्यस्थल पर लैंगिक उत्पीड़न की शिकायत दर्ज कराने की विधिक समय-सीमा (परिसीमा काल) निर्धारित की गई है:
व्यथित महिला घटना घटित होने की तिथि से 3 माह के भीतर आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) या स्थानीय समिति (LC) के समक्ष लिखित शिकायत प्रस्तुत कर सकती है। यदि घटनाओं की कोई श्रृंखला (लगातार होने वाली घटनाएं) है, तो अंतिम घटना घटित होने की तिथि से 3 माह के भीतर शिकायत दर्ज कराई जा सकती है।

महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु:
1. एकल घटना: घटना की तिथि से 3 माह की अवधि।
2. घटनाओं की श्रृंखला: निरंतर या बार-बार होने वाले उत्पीड़न के मामले में परिसीमा काल की गणना अंतिम घटना की तिथि से की जाती है।
3. अवधि विस्तार: धारा 9(1) के दूसरे परंतुक के अनुसार समिति उचित कारण दर्ज करके इस अवधि को अधिकतम 3 माह और बढ़ा सकती है।

अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Within 3 months of the incident or last incident in a series

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: incident in a series Section 9(1) stipulates that an aggrieved woman must submit a written complaint within a period of three months from the date of the incident. In cases involving a series of incidents, the complaint must be filed within three months from the date of the last occurrence in that series.

questions.question_english: A female staff member files a complaint of sexual harassment with the ICC and requests conciliation. The respondent agrees to pay her a monetary sum to drop the complaint. How should the ICC legally proceed?
options_english: Draft a formal conciliation agreement including the monetary settlement and close the proceedings
Forward the monetary settlement proposal to the District Officer for administrative approval
Inform the parties that monetary settlement cannot be the basis of conciliation
Ask the school Principal to deduct the agreed settlement amount from the respondent's salary
questions.explanation_english:
Under the proviso to Section 10(1) of the POSH Act, 2013, the statute explicitly commands:
'Provided that no monetary settlement shall be made as a basis of conciliation.'

Legal and Policy Rationale:
1. Absolute Prohibition: The law strictly bars financial transactions or monetary payouts as the foundation of conciliation to prevent wealthy or influential perpetrators from buying off complainants or monetizing workplace sexual harassment.
2. Mandatory Duty of ICC: When any monetary offer is made by the respondent or demanded during conciliation, the ICC is statutorily bound to inform both parties that financial settlements are impermissible under the Act and refuse to record or facilitate any such arrangement.
3. Permissible Terms: Conciliation may include apologies, reprimands, behavioral undertakings, or changes in supervisory/reporting arrangements.
4. Default to Inquiry: If the parties cannot reach an agreement on lawful, non-monetary terms, the ICC must terminate conciliation and proceed with a regular inquiry under Section 11.

Therefore, option (C) is the legally mandated procedure.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 10(1) का परंतुक (Proviso) स्पष्ट रूप से यह प्रावधान करता है:
'परंतु सुलह के आधार के रूप में कोई मौद्रिक समझौता नहीं किया जाएगा।'

विधिक व नीतिगत कारण:
1. पूर्ण प्रतिबंध: विधायिका ने यह प्रतिबंध इसलिए लगाया है ताकि कोई भी प्रभावशाली या संपन्न आरोपी धनबल के सहारे पीड़िता पर दबाव न बना सके या कार्यस्थल पर गरिमा के हनन को वित्तीय सौदेबाजी का रूप न दिया जा सके।
2. समिति का दायित्व: यदि सुलह के दौरान आरोपी पैसे देने की पेशकश करता है अथवा वित्तीय लेन-देन की बात आती है, तो आईसीसी को तुरंत दोनों पक्षों को अवगत कराना होगा कि कानूनन मौद्रिक समझौता पूर्णतः वर्जित है। सुलह केवल गैर-मौद्रिक शर्तों (जैसे बिना शर्त लिखित माफी मांगना, भविष्य में सभ्य आचरण का आश्वासन, कार्यस्थल या सीटिंग व्यवस्था में बदलाव आदि) पर ही आधारित हो सकती है।
3. जांच की शुरुआत: यदि गैर-मौद्रिक सुलह संभव नहीं है, तो समिति धारा 11 के तहत औपचारिक जांच शुरू करेगी।

अतः विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Inform the parties that monetary settlement cannot be the basis of conciliation

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: cannot be the basis of conciliation Section 10(1) explicitly prohibits any monetary settlement from being made the basis of conciliation between the aggrieved woman and the respondent. If a financial arrangement is proposed, the committee must inform both parties that financial transactions are impermissible under statutory conciliation rules and refuse to record such an agreement.

questions.question_english: Can a legal heir file a complaint on behalf of an aggrieved woman if she is deceased, under the provisions of the POSH Act, 2013?
options_english: Yes, provided prior written permission is granted by the ICC
Yes, as explicitly provided under Section 9(2) of the Act
No, the legal right to file a complaint extinguishes with her death
No, only the police can initiate legal action in such circumstances
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 9(2) of the POSH Act, 2013, the right of representative complaint is explicitly provided:
'Where the aggrieved woman is unable to make a complaint on account of her physical or mental incapacity or death or otherwise, her legal heir or such other person as may be prescribed may make a complaint under this section.'

Furthermore, Rule 6(iii) of the POSH Rules, 2013 stipulates that where the aggrieved woman is dead, a complaint may be filed by any person who has knowledge of the incident, with the written consent of her legal heir.

Significance of the Provision:
1. Preservation of Cause of Action: The right to departmental inquiry, accountability, and institutional justice does not abate upon death.
2. Legal Standing of Heirs: Legal heirs (such as children, surviving spouse, or parents) possess direct statutory standing to demand inquiry and compensation under Section 13/15.
3. Independent of Criminal Law: This departmental redressal operates independently of any police FIR or IPC/BNS criminal investigation.

Therefore, option (B) is explicitly authorized by Section 9(2) of the Act.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 9(2) के अनुसार:
'जहां व्यथित महिला अपनी शारीरिक या मानसिक असमर्थता अथवा मृत्यु या अन्यथा के कारण शिकायत करने में असमर्थ है, वहां उसका विधिक वारिस (लीगल हेयर) या ऐसा अन्य व्यक्ति, जो विहित किया जाए, इस धारा के अधीन शिकायत कर सकेगा।'

इसके अतिरिक्त, पॉश नियम, 2013 के नियम 6(iii) में यह व्यवस्था दी गई है कि व्यथित महिला की मृत्यु हो जाने की दशा में, घटना की जानकारी रखने वाला कोई भी व्यक्ति, मृतका के विधिक वारिस की लिखित सहमति प्राप्त करके शिकायत दर्ज करा सकता है।

विधिक महत्व:
- कार्यस्थल पर लैंगिक उत्पीड़न के मामलों में व्यथित महिला की मृत्यु हो जाने से जांच कराने और दोषी को दंडित कराने का विधिक अधिकार समाप्त नहीं होता।

questions.question_english: What is the statutory timeline within which an establishment employing 10 or more employees must constitute an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) under Section 4 of the POSH Act, 2013?

Within 3 months from the date of official notification
Within 6 months from the commencement of the academic or financial year
Within 1 year of establishing operations
questions.explanation_english:
Section 4(1) of the POSH Act, 2013 states:
'Every employer of a workplace shall, by an order in writing, constitute a Committee to be known as the Internal Complaints Committee.'
The statute provides no transition period or grace window (such as 3, 6, or 12 months) for constituting the ICC. The obligation is immediate as soon as an establishment employs 10 or more employees (or immediately upon the commencement of the Act on December 9, 2013).
Under Section 26(1)(a) of the Act, failure to constitute an Internal Complaints Committee constitutes a statutory violation punishable with a fine of up to Rs. 50,000 for the employer, and repeated failure may result in double penalty or cancellation/deregistration of the establishment's license/approval.
questions.explanation_hindi:
POSH अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 4(1) के अनुसार, प्रत्येक नियोक्ता का यह वैधानिक दायित्व है कि वह एक लिखित आदेश द्वारा 'आंतरिक शिकायत समिति' (ICC) का गठन करे।

धारा 26(1)(a) के तहत समिति गठित करने में विफलता पर नियोक्ता पर ₹50,000 तक का जुर्माना लगाया जा सकता है और बार-बार उल्लंघन करने पर मान्यता या लाइसेंस रद्द किया जा सकता है। अतः विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: If a settlement is arrived at through conciliation under Section 10 of the POSH Act, what is the mandatory next step for the ICC?
options_english: Record settlement, notify employer, and share copies with parties
Conduct a full departmental inquiry despite the recorded settlement agreement
Forward the settlement agreement directly to the local police station
Keep the settlement strictly confidential and take no further administrative action
questions.explanation_english:
Section 10 of the POSH Act, 2013 sets forth the sequential steps to be executed upon the successful completion of conciliation:
1. Recording the Settlement (Section 10(2)): The Internal Committee or Local Committee must formally record the terms of the settlement arrived at between the parties.
2. Forwarding to Employer (Section 10(2)): The committee forwards the recorded settlement to the employer (or District Officer) to implement actions as specified in the recommendations.
3. Furnishing Copies (Section 10(3)): The committee must provide authenticated copies of the recorded settlement to both the aggrieved woman and the respondent.
4. Inquiry Barred (Section 10(4)): Once a valid conciliation settlement is recorded, no further inquiry shall be conducted into the complaint by the ICC.

Note: If the respondent fails to comply with the terms of the settlement, Section 11(1) proviso allows the ICC to re-open the case and proceed with a full inquiry. Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 10 में सुलह समझौता होने के बाद की वैधानिक प्रक्रिया स्पष्ट रूप से दी गई है:
1. समझौते को अभिलिखित करना: धारा 10(2) के अनुसार, आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) दोनों पक्षों के बीच हुए समझौते के सभी नियमों एवं शर्तों को लिखित रूप में दर्ज (रिकॉर्ड) करेगी।
2. नियोक्ता को प्रेषित करना: समिति इस समझौते की रिपोर्ट नियोक्ता (विद्यालय प्रबंधन/सक्षम प्राधिकारी) को भेजेगी ताकि की गई सिफारिशों के अनुसार आवश्यक प्रशासनिक कदम उठाए जा सकें।
3. पक्षकारों को प्रतियां प्रदान करना: धारा 10(3) के अनुसार, समिति समझौते की प्रति व्यथित महिला तथा प्रत्यर्थी दोनों को अनिवार्य रूप से प्रदान करेगी।
4. अग्रिम जांच पर रोक: धारा 10(4) के तहत सुलह हो जाने पर समिति द्वारा कोई अग्रिम विभागीय जांच नहीं की जाएगी (यद्यपि धारा 11(1) के परंतुक के अनुसार यदि आरोपी समझौते की शर्तों का उल्लंघन करता है, तो जांच पुनः शुरू की जा सकती है)।

अतः विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Record settlement, notify employer, and share copies with parties

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: share copies with parties Upon reaching a settlement through conciliation under Section 10, the committee must record the agreed terms, forward the settlement record to the employer to take recommended actions, and provide copies to both parties. Once conciliation is completed, no further departmental inquiry into the complaint is conducted by the committee.

questions.question_english: During a student awareness session in a school, a student drops an anonymous note in the POCSO complaint box detailing sexual abuse perpetrated by a family member at home. What is the mandatory and immediate legal course of action for the Principal?
options_english: Disregard the anonymous note entirely on the grounds that it lacks legal credibility and documentary proof.
Attempt to identify the student's handwriting to conduct an internal private counseling session within the school.
Forward the note immediately to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or local police for official investigation.
Convene an urgent general Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) meeting to discuss the matter openly.
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 19(1) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, any person (including the Principal or Head of Institution) who has apprehension or knowledge that an offence under this Act has been committed, or is likely to be committed, is legally mandated to report the matter immediately to the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) or the local police. Even if the complaint or disclosure received via the school's POCSO complaint box or drop-box is anonymous, the institutional head cannot ignore it, nor can they initiate their own private handwriting investigation or internal fact-finding. Conducting unauthorized internal inquiries can compromise evidence and delay critical protective intervention. Furthermore, discussing allegations openly in a PTA meeting is strictly illegal and violates the confidentiality mandates under Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice Act and Section 33(7) / Section 19 of POCSO. Thus, promptly transmitting the disclosure to the SJPU / police is the only legally compliant action.
questions.explanation_hindi: लैंगिक अपराधों से बालकों का संरक्षण (पॉक्सो) अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 19(1) के तहत, किसी भी व्यक्ति (जिसमें संस्था का प्रधान या प्रधानाचार्य शामिल है) को यदि यह आशंका या जानकारी होती है कि इस अधिनियम के तहत कोई अपराध किया गया है अथवा किए जाने की संभावना है, तो वह इसकी सूचना तत्काल विशेष किशोर पुलिस इकाई (SJPU) या स्थानीय पुलिस को देने के लिए वैधानिक रूप से बाध्य है। भले ही शिकायत पेटी में प्राप्त पत्र अनाम (गुमनाम) हो, संस्था प्रमुख उसे नजरअंदाज नहीं कर सकता और न ही अपने स्तर पर हस्तलेख (हैंडराइटिंग) की जांच या अनौपचारिक पूछताछ कर सकता है। अनौपचारिक जांच से साक्ष्य नष्ट होने का खतरा रहता है और बच्चे की सुरक्षा में देरी होती है। साथ ही, PTA जैसी खुली बैठकों में चर्चा करना बच्चे की गोपनीयता का उल्लंघन है जो दंडनीय है। अतः प्रधानाचार्य का एकमात्र विधिक कर्तव्य उस पत्र को तुरंत SJPU अथवा पुलिस को अग्रेषित करना है। इसलिए विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।

questions.explanation_english: The telephone number '1098' (Ten-Nine-Eight) is the designated 24-hour, toll-free emergency phone outreach service for children in need of care and protection across India. Operating under the Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD) under Mission Vatsalya (formerly Childline India Foundation), 1098 links distressed children to emergency response, shelter, healthcare, and rehabilitation services. Mandatory guidelines from the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) and CBSE require schools to display 1098 prominently across campuses (on notice boards, student diaries, washrooms, and entry gates). questions.explanation_english: The POCSO (Amendment) Act, 2019 significantly enhanced the punishment for Aggravated Penetrative Sexual Assault under Section 6. Prior to the amendment, the minimum punishment was 10 years rigorous imprisonment. Following the 2019 amendment, Section 6 provides that whoever commits aggravated penetrative sexual assault shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life (meaning remainder of that person's natural life), and with fine, or with death. Thus, the statutory minimum penalty is now 20 years of rigorous imprisonment.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉक्सो (संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2019 द्वारा धारा 6 के तहत गुरुतर प्रवेशन लैंगिक हमले के लिए दंड को अत्यंत कठोर कर दिया गया है। 2019 के संशोधन से पूर्व इस अपराध के लिए न्यूनतम सजा 10 वर्ष का कठोर कारावास थी। संशोधित धारा 6 के अनुसार, जो कोई भी गुरुतर प्रवेशन लैंगिक हमला करेगा, उसे कम से कम बीस वर्ष के कठोर कारावास से दंडित किया जाएगा, जिसे आजीवन कारावास (उस व्यक्ति के प्राकृतिक जीवन के शेष समय तक कारावास) और जुर्माने तक, या मृत्युदंड से भी दंडित किया जा सकेगा। अतः वर्तमान में वैधानिक न्यूनतम सजा 20 वर्ष का कठोर कारावास है।

Coercing the aggrieved woman into unconditionally forgiving the respondent

questions.explanation_english:
Section 10 of the POSH Act, 2013 governs the process of conciliation:
1. Section 10(1) provides that the Internal Committee (or Local Committee) may, before initiating an inquiry under Section 11 and exclusively at the request of the aggrieved woman, take steps to settle the matter between her and the respondent through conciliation.
2. The proviso to Section 10(1) explicitly mandates that "no monetary settlement shall be made as a basis of conciliation." Any attempt to settle sexual harassment complaints through monetary compensation is strictly illegal.
3. Where a settlement has been arrived at, the committee records the settlement terms, forwards the report to the employer, and provides copies to both parties. Once conciliation succeeds, no further formal inquiry is conducted.
Thus, conciliation is an informal dispute resolution mechanism facilitated only upon the woman's voluntary written request, without monetary exchange, and without conducting a formal inquiry.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 10 के अंतर्गत 'सुलह' (समाधान) के स्पष्ट सांविधिक नियम निर्धारित हैं:
1. धारा 10(1) के अनुसार, आंतरिक समिति अथवा स्थानीय समिति धारा 11 के तहत औपचारिक जांच शुरू करने से पहले केवल व्यथित महिला के लिखित अनुरोध पर ही दोनों पक्षों के बीच सुलह के माध्यम से मामले को सुलझाने का कदम उठा सकती है। समिति या नियोक्ता महिला पर सुलह का कोई दबाव नहीं बना सकता।
2. धारा 10(1) के परंतुक में स्पष्ट प्रतिबंध है कि किसी भी मौद्रिक समझौते को सुलह का आधार नहीं बनाया जाएगा (no monetary settlement shall be made as a basis of conciliation)।
3. सुलह होने पर समिति समझौते की शर्तों का विवरण दर्ज कर नियोक्ता को भेजती है और दोनों पक्षों को प्रति देती है, जिसके बाद कोई औपचारिक जांच नहीं की जाती।
अतः सुलह एक अनौपचारिक समाधान प्रक्रिया है जो महिला के लिखित अनुरोध पर बिना किसी औपचारिक जांच या वित्तीय लेनदेन के संपन्न की जाती है। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 9 of the POSH Act, 2013, inquiry into workplace sexual harassment can only be initiated upon a written complaint submitted to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) within three months of the incident.
